references.text: Parallel to Jesus' baptismal activity in Judea, John continued to baptize at Aenon near Salim, as described in [ref:Joh 3:23|John 3:23].
Jesus' baptismal activity in Judea was noticed by the disciples of John the Baptist, who came and complained to John that everyone was now going to Jesus: [ref:Joh 3:26|John 3:26].
In [ref:Joh 4:1-3|John 4:1-3] it is clarified that it was not actually Jesus himself who baptized, but his disciples, and that he left Judea when the Pharisees heard about his activity.
Jesus' journey to the land of Judea is connected with his visit to Jerusalem for the Passover festival, mentioned in [ref:Joh 2:13|John 2:13], which shows that he was already in the Judean area.

The synoptic gospels place Jesus' public ministry in Galilee after John was imprisoned ([ref:Mark 1:14|Mark 1:14]), while the Gospel of John here shows a period when Jesus and John were active simultaneously in Judea.
John the Baptist's testimony about Jesus, given in the context of Jesus' baptismal activity in Judea, culminates with the words in [ref:Joh 3:36|John 3:36] concerning faith in the Son.
Some of the disciples who followed Jesus had first been disciples of John the Baptist, as described in [ref:Joh 1:35-37|John 1:35-37].
